div.head: VI As 1.1
div.ab: Ðæt is þonne ærest: þæt man ne sparige nánan þe[of] ofer XII pæningas ⁊ ofer XII wintre mán, þone þe wé on folcriht geáxian, þæt ful sý ⁊ to nánán andsæce ne mæge; þæt wé hine ofslean ⁊ niman eall þæt he áge; ⁊ niman ærest þæt ceapgyld of ðam yrfe, ⁊ dæle man syððan þone ofereácan on III: ænne dǽl þam wife, gif heo clæne sy ⁊ þæs fácnes gewita nære, ⁊ þæt oðer on II: to healfum fó se cyng, to healfum se ferscipe. Gif hit bocland sy oððe bisceopa land, þonne ah se landhlaford þone healfan dǽl wið þone ge[fer]scipe gemæne.

Est inprimis, ut non parcatur alicui latroni supra XII annos et supra XII den., de quo uere fuerit inquisitum, quod reus sit et ad negacionem aliquam non possit, quin occidatur et capiatur omne quod habet. Et excipiatur inprimis captale repetentis de pecunia ipsa, et diuidatur postea superplus in tres partes: unam partem habeat uxor eius, si in eo munda sit et ipsius facinoris conscia non fuerit; reliquum diuidatur in duas partes: dimidium habeat rex, dimidium societas. Si sit bocland uel biscopland (id est terra testamentalis uel episcopalis), tunc erit media pars terrę domino cum societate communis.

Ðæt is þonne ærest: Þæt man ne sparige nánan þe[ofe] ofer XII pæningas ⁊ ofer XII wintre mánn þone þe wé on folcriht geáxian, þæt [he] ful sý ⁊ to nánán andsæce ne mæge; þæt wé hine ofslean ⁊ niman eall þæt he áge; ⁊ niman ærest pæt ceapgyld of ðam yrfe, ⁊ dæle man syððan þone ofereácan on III: ænne dǽl þam wife, gif heo clæne sy ⁊ þæs fácnes gewita nære, ⁊ þæt oðer on II; to healfum fó se cyng, to healfum se ferscipe. Gif hit bocland sy oððe bisceopa land, þonne ah se landhlaford þone healfan dǽl wið þone geferscipe gemæne.

Nämlich erstens nun: dass man keinen Dieb schone, [der] über 12 Pfennige [gestohlen hat] und ein Mann über 12 Jahre [alt ist] — einen, welchen wir nach Landrecht erkennen, dass er überführt ist und zu keiner Leugnung [zugelassen werden] kann; dass wir ihn [vielmehr] erschlagen und alles, was er hat, fortnehmen, und zuerst von der Habe das Ersatzgeld [für den Bestohlenen] abziehen; und danach theile man den Überrest in drei [Theile]: einen Theil der Ehefrau — wenn sie unschuldig ist und nicht Mitwisserin jener Missethat war — und das Übrige in zwei: zur Hälfte greife der König, zur Hälfte die Genossenschaft. Wenn [des Diebes] Landgut urkundlich geliehen oder auf Bisthumsboden ist, dann erhält der [obere] Grundherr letztere Hälfte mit der Genossenschaft gemeinsam.

Namely, first of all: that we spare no thief [who has stolen] over 12 pence and [is] a man over 12 years [old] — one whom we find according to folk-law to be convicted and [who] can [be allowed] no denial; that we [rather] kill him and take everything he has, and first deduct from the property the compensation-money [for the person robbed]; and after that let the remainder be divided into three [parts]: one part to the wife — if she is innocent and was not privy to the crime — and the rest into two: let the king take half, the fellowship half. If [the thief's] land is bookland or on episcopal land, then the [superior] landlord receives the latter half jointly with the fellowship.

First of all: No thief shall be spared [who has stolen goods worth] more than twelve pence, and who is over twelve years old. If we find him guilty according to the public law, and he cannot in any wise deny it, we shall put him to death and take all he possesses; and we shall first take the value of the [stolen] goods from his possessions, and afterwards what is left shall be divided into three. One part shall be given to the wife if she is innocent and not an accessory to the crime; and the remainder shall be divided into two, the king taking one half and the [slain man's] associates the other half. If he is a tenant on land held by title deed, or on land belonging to a bishop, the owner of the land shall share equally with the associates.

First, namely: that no thief [who steals] over 12 pence and [who is] over 12 years old is to be spared, whom according to the common law we have discovered to be guilty and to be unable to deny it; we are to kill him and take all that he owns, and first we are to take the value of the [stolen] property from his possessions, and what is left is to be divided into three, one part for the wife, if she is innocent and was not privy to the crime, and the remainder [is to be divided] into two; the king is to succeed to half, the fellowship to half. If it is bookland or bishops’ land, then the lord of the estate has a right to that half part in common with the fellowship….

Die Kapitel zählt auch II As 13—18. — Alle Paragraphen des Kap. 1 bieten Reichsrecht nur mit partikularer, lokaler Exekutive
II As 13—18 also numbers the chapters. — All the paragraphs of cap. 1 contain law of the realm, merely with a particular, local executive

‘man’, gleich ‘wir’ im folgenden Satz, bed. das öffentliche Gericht. Mit dessen Umstand oder Urteilfindern aber müssen die redenden Gildegenossen persönlich oder durch Vertretung (einen aus ihnen gewählten Ausschuss?; s. Gl Gericht 20) identisch sein. Richter ist der königliche Vogt; 1, 4

‘One’, equivalent to ‘we’ in the following sentence, means the public court. With its assembly of bystanders or its judgment-finders, however, the gild-fellows who are speaking must be identical, either in person or through representation (a committee elected from among them?; see Gl Gericht 20). The judge is the king’s reeve; 1, 4

Wie der handhafte (s. d. Gl 5ff.) Dieb in II 1 wird hier der ‘offenbare’ in weiterem Sinne behandelt, nicht aber, wie in IV 6, jeder Dieb. Die Minimalgrenze ist hier von 8 auf 12 Pf. hinaufgesetzt. Unten 12, 1 wird die Strafmündigkeit auf 15 Jahre erhöht; vgl. Gl Diebstahl 9c; mündig 7. a

Like the thief caught in the act (see that word in Gl 5ff.) in II 1, the ‘manifest’ thief in a wider sense is dealt with here, but not, as in IV 6, every thief. The minimum limit is raised here from 8 to 12 pence. Below, 12, 1, the age of criminal responsibility is raised to 15 years; cf. Gl Diebstahl 9c; mündig 7. a
gerichtlich erweisen; ‘learn, erkunden’ ist zu schwach

nicht ‘nichts davon leugne’; Beklagter gelangt nicht zur Reinigung; vgl. IV As 6{e}

Das Bussgeld für klagenden Bestohlenen fällt fort, da Leibesstrafe eintritt; Schreuer Verbrechenskonk. 163. — Dieser Satz berücksichtigt den Fall, dass der Hingerichtete auf Folcland sass, der nächste den, dass er Hintersass auf Bocland war

The compensation for the robbed man who brings the charge lapses, since bodily punishment takes its place; Schreuer Verbrechenskonk. 163. — This sentence provides for the case in which the executed man sat on folkland, the next one for the case in which he was a dependent tenant on bookland
‘zwei’ Frühere nur nach Q späterer Rezension
Earlier scholars have ‘two’ only on the authority of Q’s later recension
Vgl. Gl Ehefrau 10. Die Witwe steht hier für die Kinder (Familie) des Hingerichteten
Cf. Gl Ehefrau 10. The widow here stands for the children (family) of the executed man
Ebd. 9. a; Q setzt öfter facinus für facn, durch Buchstabengleichheit verführt
Ibid. 9. a; Q often puts facinus for facn, misled by the similarity of the letters

Das Wort fera und ferscipe belegt Toller weiter nicht. — Über Grundbesitz der Genossenschaft s. d. Gl 12g. — Über diesen Anteil der Gerichtsgemeinde an der Vermögenseinziehung s. d. Gl 5e. 8a. c. In Schweden erhält von dem Eingezogenen 1/3 die Frau, 1/9 der König, 1/9 die Hundertschaft; Lehmann Königsfriede 25. Keine Parallele bietet das Bussgeld, welches geferræden vom Gildegenossen für Vergehen gegen die Gilde bezieht zu Abbotsbury; Thorpe Dipl. 606

Toller gives no further instance of the word fera or of ferscipe. — On landholding by the fellowship see that word in Gl 12g. — On this share of the court community in the confiscation of property see that word in Gl 5e. 8a. c. In Sweden, of the confiscated property the wife receives 1/3, the king 1/9, the hundred 1/9; Lehmann Königsfriede 25. No parallel is offered by the fine which the geferræden at Abbotsbury receives from a gild-fellow for offences against the gild; Thorpe Dipl. 606
Statt ‘urkundlich geliehen’ bessere Übs.: ‘[abhängig von] Bocland’; s. d. Gl 18. Keineswegs ist das Bocland ‘the scene of capture’; gegen Maitland Domesday 287
Instead of ‘lent by charter’ a better translation is ‘[dependent on] bookland’; see that word in Gl 18. The bookland is by no means ‘the scene of capture’; against Maitland Domesday 287

Der Adlige oder Bischof erhalten 1/6 zurück, das andere 1/6 bekommt die Gilde in derselben Abhängigkeit zu ihm, die der Hingerichtete trug, als Leiheland. — Anderwärts fiel alles læn (s. d. Gl 6) des Hingerichteten an den Verleiher zurück. — Wilkins versteht unrichtig den Erben des Hingerichteten. — Textlücke vermutet grundlos K. Maurer Kr. Übsch. I 112

The noble or bishop receives 1/6 back; the other 1/6 the gild obtains as leased land, in the same dependence on him in which the executed man had held it. — Elsewhere all the læn (see that word in Gl 6) of the executed man reverted to the lender. — Wilkins wrongly takes this to mean the heir of the executed man. — K. Maurer Kr. Übsch. I 112 groundlessly suspects a lacuna in the text
Prices Besserung in þone ist richtig, denn þonne geht schon vorauf; þone als Artikel verstand Q
Price’s emendation to þone is correct, for þonne has already preceded; Q understood þone as the article

Prices Besserung, die Q entspricht, ist notwendig, denn gerefscipe (s. u. 8, 4), als Vertreter des Fiskus, kann nicht neben dem König noch einmal als Teilempfänger des Konfiszierten vorkommen; auch wäre wenn das vorkäme, das Fehlen des Vogtes 4 Zeilen vorher unerklärlich

Price’s emendation, which corresponds to Q, is necessary, for gerefscipe (see below 8, 4), as representative of the fisc, cannot appear a second time alongside the king as a recipient of a share of the confiscated property; moreover, if that were the case, the absence of the reeve 4 lines earlier would be inexplicable
This chapter consists of regulations which were enforced throughout the whole nation and not merely in the locality of London. The by-laws proper of the association begin with cap. 2.
See note 1 to Alf. cap. 41. The case taken here is not that of a man who holds land by title deed, but that of a farmer who is a tenant on land which the landlord himself holds by title deed.
Liebermann understands this to mean that the landowner and the association each receive one-sixth of the property.
